name: CRT 1990s
direction:
Aesthetic directives

1990s CRT AND EARLY-DIGITAL EXPLOITATION — video feedback and crude chroma-key. Every shot must embody all of these simultaneously.

TONAL STRUCTURE AND COLOR. Cold digital palette: matte black, concrete grey, pale washed-out skin, and occasional saturated chroma-key spill. Blacks are lifted and noisy, never true crushed black. Highlights are clipped and carry a green or magenta cast from analog compression. Contrast is flat and muddy in the midtones, with harsh clipping at the extremes. The overall grade reads as early digital video with analog compression artifacts, not clean modern digital.

SURFACE. Scan-line structure from CRT monitors. Analog compression artifacts: blocking, color bleed, macroblocking at edges. Video feedback loops create recursive ghosting. Visible matte lines at chroma-key composite boundaries. The image reads as a video signal, not film. Grain is replaced by digital noise and compression blocking.

EDGE BEHAVIOUR. Edges are sharp but carry chromatic fringing and compression artifacts. Chroma-key matte edges are visible and crude — hard colored halos at composite boundaries. Scan-line ghosting creates trailing edges on moving subjects. No clean digital edges; everything carries analog-to-digital conversion imperfection.

LIGHT LOGIC. Harsh institutional or industrial lighting: fluorescent tubes, bare bulbs, cold floodlights. Light is flat and unforgiving. Chroma-key backgrounds provide flat, even, saturated color fields. Practical monitor glow may provide localized colored light. Falloff is minimal. All sources off-camera and unseen except diegetic practicals like monitors and fluorescent fixtures.

DEPTH STRATEGY. Carried by brutalist concrete architecture, exposed rebar, and fiber-optic bundles. Chroma-key creates flat, artificial background planes that contrast with real foreground depth. The image reads as a hybrid of real industrial space and crude digital composite.

COMPOSITION GRAMMAR. Hand-held kinetic drift. Asymmetrical framing. Mass sits off-center. Foreground occlusion from concrete pillars, rebar, and industrial structures. The frame may carry scan-line tearing or feedback ghosting that displaces portions of the image.

PROVENANCE MARKERS. Scan-line structure, analog compression blocking, chroma-key matte lines, video feedback ghosting, the flat muddy grade of early digital video. The image reads as footage captured on an early digital camera and processed through analog video equipment.

MOTION IMPLICATION. Scan-lines shimmer constantly. Video feedback creates slow recursive trails on moving subjects. Chroma-key spill shifts as subjects move. Monitor glow flickers. Compression artifacts pulse and shift. Any movement carries the signal-processing imperfection of early digital video.

ANTI-TROPE MANDATE.
- NO film grain. This is digital video, not film. Use scan-lines and compression artifacts instead.
- NO clean modern digital grading. Everything is muddy, compressed, and imperfect.
- NO on-screen displays, timestamps, date stamps, REC indicators, tracking bars, or OSD text baked into the footage.
- NO plastic AI skin texture. Skin must read as pale, matte, tactile with pores.

CAMERA AND FRAMING.

The supplied `camera` string is the authoritative motion — use it as written. Layer the 1990s flavor around it: hand-held kinetic drift, scan-line ghosting, chroma-key matte lines, compression artifacts, cold fluorescent lighting. Do not write cut or transition language.

SUBJECT RIGGING (critical).

Describe the physical state of the subject's face and mouth explicitly, using the supplied `rigging` value. Every subject in every shot needs one. Always end the rigging clause with exactly:
to prevent any facial babbling or lip-sync hallucinations.

PRACTICAL EFFECTS AND COSTUME.

Costume is 1990s: matte-black vinyl/PVC shifts, structured minimalist cuts. Hair is blunt bobs, layered cuts, space buns, crimped strands, slicked-back wet-look, micro-fringe. Makeup is matte brown lips, thin over-plucked brows, dark liner, pale foundation. Include the supplied `practical_effects` value. Texture note: materials must read as matte vinyl, PVC, or synthetic fabric with visible sheen.

AUDIO.

`overall_soundscape` — the physical, diegetic sounds only. CRT degauss thump, video-monitor scan hiss, fluorescent ballast buzz, footsteps on concrete, prop movement echoing in a brutalist space. NO video-feedback oscillator, NO warble. Write this richly.

`non_diegetic_music` — always exactly `N/A`.

CONTENT BOUNDARY.

All human characters are fictional adults. Human characters are fully clothed in opaque clothing. No nudity, sexual imagery, explicit sexual content, real-person likenesses, blood or gore. Animals and other non-human subjects are depicted non-sexually.

Do not write "Audio:", "Director's note:", "Storyboard:", or any timestamp bracket notation.
style_card: Early-digital video feedback and crude chroma-key. Scan-line ghosting, analog compression, brutalist concrete, matte vinyl.
